task.title: Status-reorder panel accepts drags only on dragover, the Blink accept-flag defect class
task.description:
Found during PR #105's review (the lost-drop bug, non-blocking note 3). The vocabulary status-reorder drag on the /statuses page answers only dragover with preventDefault; Blink takes the accept flag from dragenter whenever the hit-test target CHANGES under the cursor, so any future change that moves content under a stationary drag cursor (autoscroll, live reflow) can silently swallow drops there, exactly as PR #105's column autoscroll did on the board. No live bug today — the status list is short and nothing churns it mid-drag — but the defect class is open wherever a drop surface lacks a dragenter acceptance. Fix direction: route the panel's (and any other drop surface's) acceptance through a single shared destination function answering both dragenter and dragover, per the dragDestination() pattern PR #105 established, with the parity table covering the discriminating targets.

## Shipped (2026-08-16, PR #110)

One PR through a two-round adversarial execution-verified review (record on the PR), browser evidence from real Chrome over CDP.

The /statuses reorder panel now routes acceptance through one panelDropDestination(event, row, status) mirroring the board's dragDestination() - dragenter and dragover are literally the same listener, and drop asks the same question as the third reader. The discriminating targets: the dragged row itself, any row with no reorder in flight, any row during a file drag (via #109's shared draggingFiles(), reused after rebase as promised). A half-handled self-drop became an outright refusal with dragend doing the clearing.

The review caught that the class was only half-closed: the panel's bare dragleave erased the drop mark on every churn tick (real Blink churn pairs every dragenter with a dragleave) and even on plain browser events today - cursor sliding onto a button inside the marked row killed the mark while still inside the row. That is the exact lesson PR #108 taught on the board, not carried across; fixed with the board's own guard (contains(relatedTarget) + cursorWithin, genuine departures still clearing), verified against every churn-leave shape including the Firefox/Safari null-relatedTarget form, with both guard halves pinned independently. The review also forced a test onto the previously-unpinned mark-rewrite guard (proxied dataset counting writes: 20 drag events -> 1 write; measured 1 vs 19 on main) and corrected two overstated revert-table rows. Final matrix: all mutants discriminating across both rounds.

For the record: before this PR, current main still marked the panel row during a file drag - #109 guarded the board's handlers; the panel never had a guard. Residuals (accepted): Firefox/Safari unexercised - the coordinate half of the leave guard is their coverage, pinned by fake-DOM only since no rig here dispatches a real Gecko/WebKit dragleave.
